text:
Jordan L.: RFC follow-up: proposal to introduce a deferred_free ring + reclaim_token to decouple quick frees from actual page reclamation. putting this here for design feedback.

Jordan L.: motivation: frees in the hot path sometimes trigger synchronous work (evict + writeback) which spikes p99. idea is to make free() always fast and hand off expensive cleanup to background workers.

Jordan L.: sketch API:
```
ptr = alloc(size, hints)
reclaim_token = deferred_free(ptr)  // returns token or NULL if immediate reclaim
poll_reclaim(token) -> DONE | PENDING | ERROR
force_reclaim(token, timeout_ms) -> bool
get_frag_hint(token) -> size_bin  // optional
```

Maya R.: nice. how is this different from just returning ASYNC_PENDING? the token lets us track and index outstanding frees which helps per-tenant quotas.

Priya V.: fragmentation impact: if background workers batch many small frees we can coalesce into larger free ops. token could carry a size_bin and preferred coalesce group id.

Ethan C.: infra questions: 1) where are the deferred buffers stored? in host staging? an nvme queue? 2) what guarantees about durability/visibility do callers get after deferred_free returns?

Jordan L.: answers: 1) the ring just records metadata pointers; pages are moved to staging asynchronously by the offload agent. 2) once deferred_free returns a token, the caller MUST consider the ptr invalid. visibility semantics same as sync free. token is just bookkeeping.

Maya R.: we need a fast-path exemption for micro-allocs used by the decoder and KV cache. maybe alloc_hint FAST and deferred_free does immediate reclaim if hint == FAST. avoids token churn for tiny allocs.

Priya V.: agree. also suggest a reclaim_strategy flag cluster-wide: eager vs lazy vs tenant-controlled. Dedicated customers could pick eager for predictability.

Ethan C.: rolling deploy: older runtimes won't emit tokens; new runtime should accept NULL token gracefully. but what about callers that expect a token and will wait on it? must guard call sites.

Jordan L.: plan for compatibility: call sites that will use tokens must feature-flag the behavior and gracefully fallback to polling internal sync metrics if token is NULL. we'll ship a shim that maps deferred_free->OK on legacy nodes.

Maya R.: telemetry wishlist: outstanding_deferred_tokens per host, token_age_histogram, deferred_free_rate, force_reclaim_count. add an alert: token_age_p95 > 10s for more than 5m.

Priya V.: compaction integration: background worker could emit compact_hint(size_bin) which feeds into allocator's free pool compaction pipeline. that would reduce fragmentation introduced by delayed frees.

Ethan C.: eviction interplay: when KV cache references a pointer that is deferred, callers need a stable pin API: pin(ptr) returns true if still resident else false and then caller must fetch from host. Any chance we can keep stale resident pointers around until token done?

Jordan L.: two options: 1) keep a grace window where pinned retentions win (but that increases memory pressure), or 2) require callers to check pin() and handle misses. leaning to 2 for simplicity.

Maya R.: bench plan: create microbench with many tiny alloc/free in decoder loop, measure p50/p95/p99 latency, and run mixed workloads with microbatch and large-batch to see staging pressure. run canary for 48h.

Priya V.: tenant override: add tenant_policy {FORCE_SYNC, DEFER_BY_DEFAULT, MAX_PENDING_tokens}. adds predictability for enterprise.

Ethan C.: one more: add an admin endpoint to list outstanding tokens and optionally force_reclaim by token id for emergency remediation. should be rate-limited.

Jordan L.: solid. i'll update the RFC with token lifecycle diagram, state transitions (ALLOCATED -> DEFERRED -> STAGED -> RECLAIMED) and sample code for callers. will include compatibility notes and rollout steps.

Jordan L.: thanks folks. planning to turn this into a PR tomorrow. :+1:

OpsBot: deploy-scan: no blockers detected for canary rollout. schedule suggestion: canary rack-3 at 2026-04-02T01:00Z. monitor #release-war-room.
